title: Cluster bounce + quick capacity fixes (personal TODO)
content:
Quick brain-dump / checklist for the cluster bounce and a few small capacity/network fixes I want to finish before handoff. Mostly for my shift — rough, step-by-step + commands I actually use.

2026-03-13 morning run (notes to self)
- Goal: soft-restart nodepool-a (eu-west-1) to pick up kernel/security patch without massive eviction spike.
- Also: patch small VPC route flapping seen last night (route-table-7b) and restart sidecar injector on critical-serving namespace.

Top-level plan (high level)
1) Drain low-priority pods from nodepool-a: label selectors + cordon, then drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
2) Sequentially restart nodes (max 2 at a time, let autoscaler maintain pool).
3) Watch qps/latency on canary route (canary-serving-app) and abort if tail-lat > 200ms for > 2mins.
4) Re-enable scheduling and uncordon after health checks pass.

Checklist (commands I ran / will run)
- pre-checks:
  - kubectl get nodes -l pool=nodepool-a -o wide  # list targets
  - ./scripts/check-gpu-util.sh nodepool-a | tee /tmp/nodepool-a-util.txt  # make sure not too many running jobs
  - aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=nodepool-a*" --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,State.Name,Tags]'

- drain flow (example)
  - kubectl cordon <node>
  - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=15m || echo "drain failed for <node> - escalate"
  - watch -n10 'kubectl get pods -n critical-serving --field-selector=status.phase!=Running'

- restart flow
  - ssh ubuntu@<node-ip> 'sudo /sbin/reboot'  (use bastion: ssh -J bastion)
  - wait for node to rejoin: kubectl get nodes | grep <node> && kubectl describe node <node> | grep Ready

Health checks / metrics to watch (live dashboards + PromQL)
- canary route: sum(rate(requests_total{route="canary-serving-app"}[1m])) by (instance)  --> want throughput stable
- tail latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[2m])) by (le))  -- alert if > 0.2s for 2m
- GPU eviction count: increase in kube_pod_eviction{reason="OutOfResources"}  (should be zero)

Edge case notes (less polished)
- If node fails to come back after reboot > 15m: escalate to SRE rotation, open a quick ticket with instance-id and cloud-init logs. Probably a driver/kernel hang that needs re-image.
- If autoscaler overshoots and spins up extra instances: check autoscaler logs, decrease desired by scaling down the ASG and re-evaluate.
- If route-table-7b still flaps after reattach, it's probably SG overlap with cross-account peer; ask network to re-run BGP/neigh verify.

Small network fix (what I changed last night, note for handoff)
- Problem: flapping routes observed 03/12 23:40-00:10 UTC. Suspected: transient BGP withdraws from partner VPC.
- Quick mitigation I applied: increased route propagation timeout on RT-7b from 30s -> 120s (temporary).
- Follow-up: remind network to run full BGP session dump and escalate if pattern repeats.

Open todos (for tomorrow or handoff)
- [ ] Add small cron job to scrape node GPU temperature every 5m and post to /internal-metrics (ticket INFRA-2945)
- [ ] Add notebook with pre-bounce checklist and rollback steps in Confluence (link to add)
- [ ] Validate new sidecar-injector image (sha: sha256:abc123...) in staging before promoting to prod; create PR for deployment yaml.

Random notes to self (shortcuts, reminders)
- If draining long-running training pods, use --pod-selector='app!=training-highmem' to avoid evicting expensive jobs.
- Slack helper: /remind @on-call to watch canary at +10m after I uncordon nodes.
- If GPU driver fails to bind: systemctl status nvidia-driver.service and check /var/log/nvidia-installer.log

Handoff blurb (what I will say in Slack)
- "Just restarted 2 nodes in nodepool-a. No elevated tail-latency observed for canary route (0.99p ~ 120ms). I increased route-table-7b propagation timeout to 120s as a temporary mitigation; network team please follow up. Leaving notes here: INFRA-2891. Ping me if you see evictions or >200ms tail-latency."

Quick timeline sketch (for runbook)
- 09:00 - pre-checks complete
- 09:10 - cordon and drain node-a-03
- 09:25 - reboot triggered node-a-03
- 09:45 - node rejoined, run smoke tests, uncordon
- 09:55 - repeat for node-a-04 (max 2 simultaneous down)

node-a-02  | Ready   | 5%       | 2026-03-09 18:05
node-a-03  | NotReady| 0%       | -
node-a-04  | Ready   | 0%       | 2026-03-11 11:44

End — leaving this in Drive so I can copy into Confluence later and to make sure handoff has a single source.

Notes: intentionally terse, contains scratch commands; if anything here looks like bad practice, fix in final runbook.
